thread.title: Sen. John Hoeven Buys Apple Stock, Sells AT&T, DowDuPont, FedEx

title: Sen. John Hoeven Buys Apple Stock, Sells AT&T, DowDuPont, FedEx
text:
Sen. John Hoeven Buys Apple Stock, Sells AT&T, DowDuPont, FedEx By Jan. 15, 2019 10:14 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Joe Raedle/Getty Images Text size
Jon Hoeven, the Republican senator representing North Dakota, began 2019 by buying beaten-down shares of Apple , according to a disclosure form he filed on Friday.
Hoeven purchased between $50,001 and $100,000 of Apple (ticker: AAPL) stock on Jan. 4. Disclosure requirements don’t include specific values, only ranges.
It was his first recorded purchase or sale of shares in the iPhone maker since he bought between $50,001 and $100,000 in the stock three years ago . Hoeven could have bought and sold small batches of Apple stock during that time, however; transactions valued at $1,000 or less aren’t required to be reported.
Hoeven’s holdings in Apple stock were valued at between $250,001 and $500,000 at the end of 2017, the date of his latest annual report .
On Dec. 27, Hoeven also bought Blackstone Group (BX) stock valued at between $100,001 and $250,000. He hadn’t owned any shares of the investment manager at the end of 2017; it was his first recorded transaction in Blackstone stock since then.
The senator changed course on DowDuPont (DWDP), selling $50,001 to $100,000 of shares of the chemical giant on Dec. 27. In two different transactions in March, Hoeven had bought a total of $100,000 to $200,000 in DowDuPont stock .
His latest transaction appears to be a case of selling into weakness, as the price of the shares slipped 17% between the end of March and the close on the day he sold.
Another slumping stock Hoeven has turned to selling is FedEx (FDX). He unloaded $15,001 to $50,000 of shares of the logistics giant on Dec. 27. The senator had purchased $50,001 to $100,000 of FedEx stock only a few months before , on Sept. 19. Based on the closing prices on the days he bought and sold, the stock lost a third of its value.
Hoeven sold $15,001 to $50,000 of AT&T (T) stock, also on Dec. 27. He had sold AT&T stock valued at between $50,001 and $100,000 on May 23, and bought between $50,001 and $100,000 of shares on June 27 .
“Senator Hoeven’s stock trades were made in consultation with his financial advisers and in accordance with Senate regulations and reporting requirements,” his Senate office said in response to a request for comment on the trades.
Earlier this month , Hoeven was selected to again serve as chairman of both the Senate Indian Affairs Committee and the Senate Agriculture Appropriations Committee. He has been in both posts since January 2017.
